thread:
maria: Heads-up — after swapping to kernel kopt-v2 yesterday, I'm seeing intermittent streaming stalls for long responses on /v2/chat (model=r-1.2). Client-side chunk gaps ~120–250ms, but server token emit histograms look unchanged. Repro: send a 512->1024 token prompt and watch the chunk cadence. Sample server log:
```
[2026-03-17T22:34:12Z] emit token idx=212 latency=3.4ms kernel=kopt-v2
[2026-03-17T22:34:12Z] emit token idx=213 latency=3.6ms kernel=kopt-v2
[2026-03-17T22:34:12Z] transport chunk id=xyz size=320 tokens gap=180ms
```
Anyone seen this pattern?

aj: Hmm. Can you paste the PromQLs you're using for p95 emit vs client gaps? Also include route labels.

maria: Pasted the queries I'm running locally — they're noisy but show the delta.
```
avg by(route) (histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_server_emit_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)))

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_client_chunk_gap_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))

avg_over_time(redwood_client_last_chunk_ts - redwood_server_last_emit_ts[5m])
```
On route=/v2/chat p95(server_emit)=~4.2ms, p95(client_chunk_gap)=~185ms, avg delta ~= 160ms over the last 30m.

devon: Two quick hypotheses: 1) KV cache hot-shard evictions cause occasional kernel fallback/warmup -> transport stalls; 2) kopt-v2 changed batching heuristics (coalescing) and sometimes waits for extra tokens before emitting a chunk, which shows up as a client-side gap even though per-token emit is low. Check these metrics: `redwood_kv_eviction_rate`, `redwood_kernel_fallbacks_total`, `redwood_batch_wait_time_seconds`. Also add per-token span `emit_stage` in traces to separate kernel emit vs transport/serialize.

priya: I created a temporary Grafana board (link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/streaming/emit-vs-transport) and added panels: per-route p50/p95/p99 for `server_emit_latency`, `client_chunk_gap`, `batch_wait_time`. Also added a histogram for `chunk_size_tokens`. I'm going to add an alert: if p95(client_chunk_gap) > 100ms for a route for 5m -> page on-call. Draft alert rule:
```
alert: StreamingChunkGapHigh
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_client_chunk_gap_bucket[5m])) by (le, route)) > 0.1
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "High streaming chunk gaps on {{ $labels.route }}"
```
Will refine threshold after more data.

maria: Also attaching a tiny capture from the client (timestamps are ms since epoch):
```
client_recv: [1679074452000, 1679074452180, 1679074452365, 1679074452546]
server_emit: [1679074451998, 1679074452001, 1679074452005, 1679074452009]
// shows big transport gaps after sequence idx=2
```
This matches the 160ms delta above.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollback of kopt-v2 -> kopt-v1 initiated at 2061003000 by aj :arrows_counterclockwise:

maria: Quick follow-up after rollback — p95(client_chunk_gap) on /v2/chat dropped from ~185ms -> ~45ms within ~10m. Looks like the kernel swap triggered this regression.

aj: Thanks — filing follow-up ticket RINF-3421: add per-token emit trace spans, granular batch-wait metrics per kernel variant, and a canary plan for kernel swaps (split traffic by model-version + route).

maria: Good plan. For the immediate next deploy we should: 1) enable per-token spans in staging, 2) add a dashboard panel comparing `redwood_batch_wait_time_seconds{kernel=~"kopt-.*"}` across kernels, and 3) keep rollback playbook handy.

devon: I'll instrument `kv_eviction_rate` with a label for shard_id and add a small sampled trace on eviction events.

priya: I'll tune the alert thresholds and add an annotation that points to the rollback runbook.

aj: Closing the thread for now — thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:
